title: Check Engine - Yellow Warning
shortDescription: General ECM fault; reduced-performance mode possible.
fullDescription:
A yellow Check Engine indicates a stored diagnostic trouble code (DTC) that is not immediately critical. Common triggers include sensor faults, knock, or intermittent misfires. The engine usually runs but may enter Guardian mode.

Pull codes with VesselView or a Mercury-compatible scanner. Gasoline safety: never smoke around fuel and keep the bilge blower running.

fixSteps.title: Read DTC
fixSteps.instruction: Connect VesselView / DDT / CDS to read stored codes.

fixSteps.title: Address specific code
fixSteps.instruction: Follow service manual for the specific DTC.

whenToCallPro: If the code points to an injector, high-pressure pump, or internal engine issue.
videoSearchQuery: Mercury outboard check engine code read

faq.a: Yes at reduced RPM, but address promptly.

title: Scheduled Maintenance Due
shortDescription: ECM hour counter triggered service reminder.
fullDescription:
Mercury ECMs track run hours and trigger a reminder at service intervals (100 hour, annual, etc.). This is informational, not a fault.

Reset the reminder after completing service via VesselView.

fixSteps.title: Perform service
fixSteps.instruction: Change oil, filters, spark plugs per schedule.

whenToCallPro: For unfamiliar boaters or valve-clearance checks.

title: Engine Overheat Alarm
shortDescription: Coolant temp exceeded limit; engine in Guardian mode.
fullDescription:
Triggered by raw-water pump failure, blocked intake, or stuck thermostat. Guardian reduces RPM to protect the engine.

Stop, check the tell-tale water stream, and inspect the intake.

fixSteps.title: Stop immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Return to idle and check tell-tale stream.

fixSteps.title: Clear intake
fixSteps.instruction: Remove weeds/bag from lower unit intake.

fixSteps.title: Replace impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Annual service item; replace if tell-tale is weak.

faq.q: Can I run with weak tell-tale?
faq.a: No, damage can be extensive and fast.

title: Low Oil Pressure Warning
shortDescription: Engine oil pressure below safe threshold.
fullDescription:
Critical alarm - possible low oil level, pump failure, or sensor issue. Guardian reduces RPM and may shut down.

Stop the engine, check oil level immediately.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect dipstick; top off with correct grade.

fixSteps.title: Test sender
fixSteps.instruction: If oil is full, test/replace pressure sender.

whenToCallPro: If oil is full and sender replacement does not clear it.
videoSearchQuery: Mercury outboard low oil pressure fix

faq.a: Helps but does not guarantee - shut it down.

title: Low Battery Voltage
shortDescription: System voltage below 11.5 V at engine.
fullDescription:
Below the threshold the ECM may not maintain full function. Causes include alternator fault, corroded terminals, or aging battery.

Inspect charging voltage at idle (should be 13.8-14.4 V).

fixSteps.title: Clean terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean battery posts and cables.

fixSteps.title: Test battery
fixSteps.instruction: Load-test the battery; replace if weak.

fixSteps.title: Check charge output
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at battery with engine at 1500 RPM.

videoSearchQuery: Mercury outboard battery low voltage fix

faq.q: Can I run with low voltage?
faq.a: Briefly; risk of stalling and sensor faults rises.

title: Water Detected in Fuel/Water Separator
shortDescription: Water separator sensor triggered; drain required.
fullDescription:
Water accumulation in the separator bowl can damage injectors. Gasoline in water separator is a fire risk - drain at dock, away from ignition sources, with bilge ventilation.

Replace filter annually or when alarm triggers.

fixSteps.title: Drain separator
fixSteps.instruction: With engine off and at dock, open drain and collect water into a container. Dispose properly.

whenToCallPro: If fuel quality is questionable, have tank polished.
videoSearchQuery: Mercury outboard water in fuel drain

faq.q: Can I run with the alarm on?

title: Trim/Tilt Fluid Low
fullDescription:
Low trim fluid reduces power trim performance and can let air into cylinders. Often indicates an external seal leak.

Use Mercury Power Trim & Steering Fluid or Type F ATF.

fixSteps.title: Top off fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Fill trim reservoir to full mark.

videoSearchQuery: Mercury outboard trim fluid low fix

faq.a: Mercury PTS fluid or Type F ATF.

title: Shift Interrupt Switch Fault
shortDescription: Shift interrupt circuit not behaving as expected.
fullDescription:
Mercury digital shift momentarily cuts ignition to relieve gear pressure. A faulty sensor/switch causes rough shifts or DTCs.

Usually a sensor replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Per service manual, replace shift interrupt switch.

whenToCallPro: If DTC persists after sensor replacement.

faq.q: Can I run with rough shifts?
faq.a: Short term yes; long-term wears gears.

title: Electronic Key/Dongle Missing
shortDescription: Mercury Theft Deterrent System (MTDS) cannot read key.
fullDescription:
MTDS or keyless systems will refuse to start without the key fob in range or the ignition switch registered.

Replace key battery or re-program fob.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer CDS/G3 to program new key.

videoSearchQuery: Mercury outboard no key detected fix

title: Charging System Fault
fullDescription:
ECM monitors charge voltage. A stator or regulator failure triggers a fault; battery will discharge over time.

Test stator output per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Test output
fixSteps.instruction: Measure stator AC output at RPM per manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace part
fixSteps.instruction: Replace regulator or stator as indicated.

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
The MAP sensor informs the ECM of manifold pressure for fueling. A fault typically produces poor idle, hesitation, and a stored DTC.

Replace the sensor after verifying vacuum lines and harness.
whenToCallPro: If leak is in intake manifold.

faq.a: Usually not; engine runs in limp mode.

title: Throttle Position Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
TPS informs the ECM of throttle opening. On DTS engines a fault will send the engine to idle only until resolved.

Calibrate or replace TPS.

title: Camshaft Position Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
Without cam signal the ECM cannot sync injection. The engine may start but run roughly or fail to start.

Replace sensor and check for metallic debris on the sensor tip.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clean mounting area, install new sensor.

whenToCallPro: If debris indicates timing chain wear.

title: Crank/Engine Speed Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
Crank sensor provides RPM and timing reference. Loss = no-start. Check the sensor and harness; debris on the trigger wheel is possible.

Replace sensor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove, inspect tip and magnet for debris.

faq.a: Usually no if crank sensor is dead.

title: Detonation / Knock Detected
fullDescription:
Common from low-octane fuel, carbon buildup, or over-advanced timing. ECM retards timing to protect the engine.

Fuel with correct octane and consider a decarb treatment.

fixSteps.title: Decarb engine
fixSteps.instruction: Use Mercury Power Tune or equivalent per directions.

whenToCallPro: If knock persists with proper fuel.

faq.a: Yes - can crack pistons if ignored.
